name: Ambient loop to full track: split the chord progression into single-chord clips, intro from the loop, slower evolving section -> 'chorus' with faster chord changes -> slow outro; per-layer slow movement (band-pass pad filter with two LFOs, random LP and comb on the atmos, slow auto-pan), cutoff 'spikes' on the bass drone, arpeggiator rate automated whole -> half -> quarter -> eighth notes for energy, a double-speed drum clip and an arpeggiated pluck bass replacing the drone in the peak
goal: Expand a finished ambient loop into a structured track by turning it into rearrangeable single-chord clips and using rhythmic density as the energy control: the arp's note rate steps up from whole notes to eighths as sections intensify, the chorus changes chords more often, drums go double-time by scaling the clip to 50%, and an arpeggiated pluck bass takes over from the drone at the peak. Delta vs our loop-to-song variants: arp-rate and harmonic-rhythm as the section energy dials.

source.title: Turn an Ambient Loop into a Full Track in Bitwig Studio (Part 2)

prerequisites: DAW with clip launcher or loop regions, automation and clip time-scaling
Synth with arpeggiator, filters with modulators, comb filter, auto-pan/utility

inputs.name: loop
inputs.description: Finished ambient loop: pad, atmos, bass drone, arp pluck, drum clip

outputs.name: arrangement
outputs.description: Intro, evolving section, chorus-like peak, outro

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Drums early (Matt's taste) overrides the source's slow start: bring the drum clip in by about count 8 even in the evolving section; keep the double-time clip for the peak.
Modulators move filters/pan only, not pitch.
Mute the drone while the pluck bass plays so they do not compete.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Duplicate the loop to a clip slot and cut the chord progression into single-chord clips (consolidate each first).
Make a 16-bar intro from the loop scene.

Pad: band-pass (2-pole) filter with two independent slow LFOs on frequency and resonance. Atmos: smooth slow random modulator (unipolar, subtle) on a low-pass cutoff, a comb filter with a slow LFO on feedback and smooth random on frequency, and a very slow bipolar LFO on pan.
steps.expect: Each layer moves slowly on its own

steps.action: Automate the bass drone's oscillator cutoff in short 'spikes', copy the automation along the timeline and vary level/shape.
Arrange: slower evolving section, then a chorus-like section with more frequent chord changes and higher dynamics, then a slower outro.
Automate the arpeggiator rate: whole notes in the slow section, then half, quarter and eighth notes as energy rises (eighths in the chorus).
Duplicate the drum clip and scale it to 50% length for a double-time peak section; sprinkle squelch hits, moving them by octaves for faster/slower squelches.
For the peak, add an arpeggiated pluck bass fed with the pad chords (tune its ratio/octave lower for depth) and mute the bass drone there; finish with lightly EQ'd, delayed, reverbed one-shots.
steps.expect: Peak section with a moving bass

verification: Arp rate automation increases step-wise toward the peak and drops in the outro.
Peak section has the double-time drum clip and no drone/pluck-bass overlap.
